medicina.titulo: Drug ads can influence AI treatment recommendations, study finds
medicina.resumo: As people increasingly turn to artificial intelligence (AI) for health information, a new study by researchers at the Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai raises questions about what happens when commercial advertising appears alongside a clinical question. The findings were reported in the Nov. 11 online issue of The Lancet Digital Health.

medicina.titulo: New clinical definition outperforms BMI in diagnosing obesity
medicina.resumo: A new diagnostic definition of obesity outperforms body mass index (BMI) in identifying differences in health and prognosis, including mortality risk, according to a large international study published in Nature.

medicina.titulo: Human neurons regain communication in motor neuron disease lab models
medicina.resumo: A novel potential treatment approach for motor neuron disease (MND), similar to the approach being pursued with an investigational drug that recently entered human clinical trials, has been shown to restore broken communication between neurons in lab models of the disease. This could have beneficial therapeutic implications for 97% of people with MND, for whom there is currently no significant disease-modifying treatment.

medicina.titulo: Molecular brace traps two cancer-driving proteins to suppress prostate cancer growth in preclinical tests
medicina.resumo: Many modern cancer drugs typically target a specific protein or signaling pathway to treat tumors. Now, researchers at the University of Michigan Health Rogel Cancer Center are taking a new approach by throwing a molecular wrench into the machinery driving prostate cancer. In preclinical studies, this new approach demonstrated greater antitumor activity while sparing normal cells.

biologia.titulo: Even cacti are severely threatened in a warmer, drier world
biologia.resumo: Findings from a study spanning the Americas show that climate change forecasts are underestimating threats to biodiversity—even to exceptionally resilient species—by not factoring in extreme weather events that become more likely in a warmer world.

biologia.titulo: Nuclear softening at an embryo's two-cell stage may be vital for further embryonic development
biologia.resumo: A research team led by Kyushu University and the National Institute of Genetics has discovered that during the two-cell stage of mouse embryonic development, the embryo's nucleus softens and deforms. This nuclear softening is an integral part of major zygotic gene activation, where approximately 2,000 genes necessary for embryonic development activate simultaneously. This indicates that nuclear softening is a critical step for further embryonic development.

biologia.titulo: New review explores how faint 'glow' from plants could transform global monitoring of photosynthesis
biologia.resumo: A faint glow emitted by plants as they absorb sunlight could offer scientists a powerful new way to monitor photosynthesis across the planet. Fully realizing that potential, however, will require advances in both the general understanding of plant biology and the satellite technology used to observe it.

biologia.titulo: Cacti are severely threatened by drought in a warming world
biologia.resumo: Nature, Published online: 11 November 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-03496-z Forecasts of the effects that climate change will have on biodiversity typically rely on long-term climate averages while excluding extreme events. Projections that include severe drought predict that a majority of the 993 cactus species assessed will see large losses of suitable climatic area: more than 25% of species could lose at least 80% of it by 2100.

software.titulo: [$] Additional hardening for the glibc dynamic linker
software.resumo: The Node.js project recently had a security vulnerability that affected its Brotli decoder. The bug was a buffer overflow , but the particular way that official Node.js binaries are built for Linux meant that one of the main protections against turning a buffer overflow into remote code execution, address space layout randomization (ASLR) could not be turned on. If ASLR had been enabled, the bug would still be exploitable in theory, but much more difficult to exploit in practice. In response, the GNU C Library (glibc) is considering a new set of tunable settings to allow administrators to forbid programs that do not support ASLR. The new settings, while a welcome hardening measure, may not address the root problem.

hardware.titulo: Adeus aos 16 núcleos: novo chiplet da AMD abre caminho para Ryzen 9 de 24 núcleos
hardware.resumo: Se tem uma barreira que não parecia que seria superada, era o teto de 16 núcleos nos modelos Ryzen 9 , algo praticado há anos pela AMD. No entanto, a chegada da arquitetura Zen 6 promete quebrar essa limitação histórica. Ao reformular a estrutura de seus novos chips e expandir a densidade dos Core Complex Dies (CCDs) , a AMD prepara o terreno para introduzir uma nova era de desempenho multithread, abrindo caminho para processadores de até 24 núcleos no mercado para o consumidor final. A mudança pode representar o maior salto geracional de performance da empresa desde a estreia da microarquitetura Zen original . O avanço não se limita a colocar mais núcleos no encapsulamento, mas sim a reestruturar a forma como o chip gerencia memória cache, frequências de operação e eficiência energética. Vale ressaltar que a AMD ainda não tocou no assunto Ryzen Zen 6, então tudo aqui não passa de especulação baseada no que o próprio Time Vermelho disse em evento recente. computadores_pessoais.resumo: Windows allows you to create multiple desktops, so that users can quickly switch between a work environment, a personal one, and a desktop optimized for gaming. This often leads to overlap: a word processor, for example, is normally needed for both work and personal correspondence. If the program is running in full-screen mode, it’s often hard to tell which desktop you’re currently on. The simplest method is to assign a different background to each desktop. However, this must be a background image; Windows applies solid colors uniformly across all desktops. The Windows Virtual Desktop Helper tool always displays which desktop you are currently working on in the taskbar. You can specify exactly how this is displayed in the settings. Foundry And, of course, the wallpaper trick only works if you’re not using the current application in full-screen mode. The open-source program Windows Virtual Desktop Helper offers a better solution. But what if you’re just a regular home user? Are these additional features worth paying a bit more? Here’s what you need to consider. inteligencia_artificial.titulo: When Does It Actually Make Sense to Put AI Into Products?
inteligencia_artificial.resumo: Over the past few years, the tech industry has rushed to plug a new microchip into every device on the assumption that if you can add AI, you should. Smart vision toothbrushes , mood-reading household robots , and a host of physical products are invading consumers’ daily lives, reliant on artificial intelligence to learn, predict, and adjust our behavior. But as anyone who’s struggled to update the firmware in their fridge knows, AI doesn’t improve every product. Some product designers are asking where the line is between genuine innovation and a solution looking for a problem. Savannah Kunovsky leads a team of industrial product designers at Ideo , a design consultancy based in San Francisco focused on helping clients unpack when AI becomes a barrier rather than a breakthrough. Kunovsky spoke with IEEE Spectrum about the pressure to integrate AI in everything, where that integration goes wrong, and what companies can do to determine when an AI integration is—and isn’t—a smart choice. ciberseguranca.titulo: Malware que lê e-mails do Gmail mantém acesso mesmo após usuário desconectar conta
ciberseguranca.resumo: Um novo malware chamado Remus Stealer consegue manter o acesso à caixa de entrada do Gmail mesmo após a vítima trocar a senha, fechar o navegador ou desconectar os dispositivos da conta. A ferramenta do tipo infostealer é comercializada por cibercriminosos por US$ 1.000 mensais e promete acesso contínuo às mensagens de contas comprometidas. Segundo um relatório da empresa de cibersegurança Hudson Rock, o programa utiliza uma técnica que manipula a memória do navegador e contorna os mecanismos de segurança do Google. Em vez de roubar cookies tradicionais, a principal hipótese dos pesquisadores é que o malware obtenha uma autorização reutilizável a partir de uma sessão ativa do Gmail. Com isso, um componente remoto continua solicitando novas mensagens aos servidores do Google mesmo se o computador for desligado ou se os acessos forem revogados. Os pesquisadores ressalvam, contudo, que os detalhes exatos de como o invasor contorna as verificações antifraude n ão foram revelados pelo desenvolvedor .
